title: Asteraceae Essentials
description: Learn the defining structures and vocabulary of the sunflower family.

lessons.title: The flower head
lessons.body: What looks like one flower is usually a cluster of many tiny flowers called florets. Together they form a dense head called a capitulum.
lessons.definition: A compact inflorescence composed of many sessile florets attached to a shared receptacle.
lessons.memoryTip: Think: a capital city gathers many people; a capitulum gathers many florets.

lessons.title: Ray and disc florets
lessons.body: Many Asteraceae heads contain strap-shaped ray florets around the edge and tubular disc florets in the center. Some species have only one of these forms.
lessons.definition: A floret with a strap-shaped corolla, commonly positioned around the outside of the head.
lessons.memoryTip: Rays radiate outward; discs fill the center.

lessons.title: Bracts and the involucre
lessons.body: A ring or series of modified leaves called bracts surrounds and supports the flower head. Collectively, these bracts form the involucre.
lessons.definition: The group of bracts surrounding and supporting a flower head.
lessons.memoryTip: The involucre is the wrapper around the flower head.

lessons.title: Fruit and dispersal
lessons.body: Asteraceae commonly produce a dry, one-seeded fruit called a cypsela. A modified calyx called the pappus may form hairs, scales, or bristles that help disperse it.
lessons.definition: A modified calyx on a cypsela that can aid seed dispersal.
lessons.memoryTip: The fluffy part of a dandelion is its pappus.

questions.prompt: In the Asteraceae family, what is the name of the dense flower head composed of many individual florets?
questions.explanation: The entire dense head is called a capitulum. It may look like one flower, but it contains many florets.

questions.prompt: Which florets are typically strap-shaped and positioned around the edge of the flower head?
questions.hint: Their shape appears to radiate outward.
questions.explanation: Ray florets commonly form the petal-like outer ring; disc florets are usually tubular and central.

questions.prompt: What is the collective name for the bracts that surround and support an Asteraceae flower head?
questions.hint: Think of the wrapper around the flower head.
questions.explanation: The supporting bracts collectively form the involucre.

questions.prompt: What is the modified calyx that may help disperse an Asteraceae fruit?
questions.hint: It creates the familiar fluff on a dandelion.
questions.explanation: The pappus can form hairs, scales, or bristles that aid dispersal.

questions.prompt: Describe where ray florets and disc florets are usually located in a typical sunflower-like head.
questions.answer: Ray florets are around the edge and disc florets are in the center.

questions.explanation: Ray florets generally occupy the outer edge, while tubular disc florets occupy the center.
